answer.generated: Executing code within a sandbox environment allows the Java or C# code to run safely inside the database query execution process, accessing its own memory while being isolated from the rest of the system. This approach reduces the overhead of interprocess communication, which can be costly in terms of CPU cycles, especially on modern architectures where communication delays are significant. By running code locally, the system avoids the latency associated with remote procedure calls, thereby improving performance for queries that incorporate external logic.
